Baked potato advice+ budgeted uni student/ hostel recipes needed. Lil bros I’ve been on a weight loss journey and potatoes have been my best friend. It keeps me full, great source of fiber and carbs and I’ve been able to loose 22kg while eating like 400g of potatoes everyday. Usually I air fry them. I’ve baked potatoes in the air fryer and obviously if u trying to make it as low cal as possible ur gonna avoid fat sources but rn im open to trying any advice on how to make it better or any suggestions u think would be great toppings. Usually I just air fry it with a very tiny amount of oil, then put some peri peri sauce and add mozerella cheese and that’s it. But with what’s I’ve been seeing people post mine looks nothing like that 😭 mine usually comes out kinda dry and u know how everyone else’s has a cut in the middle and they load it with topping? Kinda like jacket potatoes? They mix the inside out with butter and it becomes this smooth texture (I haven’t tried this cuz again I wanted the cals low but I think I’ll try it now) mine never comes like that. Like my potatoes are fully cooked just kinda…idk grainy? And cuz of this I can’t get the ‘jacket’ look to it cuz the inside is stiff and grainy so rather than a slit I have to cut it in half completely. Is it just that I’m not adding butter? Is the air fryer drying it out too much? When putting it in the air fryer I usually poke holes in the potatoes and that’s it. should I wrap it in aluminium foil? Should I still stick with the airfryer or go with the oven? Does it even matter aren’t they technically the same? Do lmk what u guys think and if u have any suggestions on what I should add on top.

Smoked Beets. I started by peeling the beets (being very careful not to stain things) so I could get the seasoning deep into the root vegetable. The seasoning was applied with olive oil & consisted of kosher salt, #10 & #16 mesh black pepper, raw sugar, garlic powder, season salt, adobo powder, chipotle powder, celery seed, sumac, & arbol powder. I smoked the beets on my Weber Smoky Mountain smoker at 300F on the lower rack with the water pan removed using a mix of lump charcoal & mesquite wood for around 2 hours until they reached 205-210F internal temperature. After the beets were cooked I wrapped them in foil with a garlic/thyme compound butter then placed them in my toaster oven set to 150F until everything else was done cooking. I served these beets alongside asparagus & pork loin with a wine sauce. This was my first time roasting beets & I’ll definitely do it again. It’s way more similar in taste to a potato than I expected (almost 1:1) so the only thing I’d really advise other first timers is: more butter & more salt than you might think. If you’ve never tried smoked or grilled beets this might be one to add to your repertoire.
